alignments.note: Comparative adverb rendered *as*.
Intensifying καί realized by *also* (rules 55, 65). Rule 82 does not apply: it governs a καί answering a comparative with an English *so*, and the ASV writes none here.
Inflected verb takes its subject and auxiliary as helpers (rules 7, 9); head on the lexical verb.
Accusative object.

Preposition realized by the English preposition heading the phrase (rule 36). Rule 94 forbids a compound unit here, the ASV writing two words; rule 34 does not apply, since *in* is a real preposition answering to ἀπό rather than the adverb's own particle.
Anarthrous noun, no determiner supplied.
Complementizer written out as *that*; rule 43's test is the English, and a word is present.
Predicate noun; the Greek expresses ἐσμεν, so no copula is supplied in this clause.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive *your*; the Greek is anarthrous, so no article competes.
Expressed copula with its supplied subject pronoun as a rule 7/9 helper; head on the verb.
καθάπερ → *even as*, headed on *as*, the word the corpus spends on the comparative adverb; *even* is an intensifying helper (rules 7, 82).

Intensifying καί realized by *also*, exactly as at s002. Rule 82's correlative reading needs an English *so*, which the ASV does not write in this clause; rules 55 and 65 give the particle whatever word answers to it.

Bare subject pronoun of the verbless comparative. Rule 56's spelled-out arm (καθὼς ἡμεῖς ἕν → *even as we are one*) puts the supplied copula on the expressed predicate, not the subject; reading *ours* as a noun-phrase predicate under rule 53's exception would move *are* here, so the unit is hedged with s014.

Elliptical comparative with an expressed predicate token: the predicate carries the supplied copula (rules 53, 56), headed on *ours*. Rule 53's noun-phrase exception is doubtful here — its rationale is that an article-plus-noun predicate leaves nothing inside it for the copula, which a one-word *ours* does not do — but that reading stays defensible and would give *are* to ὑμεῖς.
Expressed preposition realized by *in* (rule 36); the article therefore keeps a bare *the* rather than a rule 21 *in the* bundle.
Article surfaces as *the* (rule 19).
Head noun of the prepositional phrase.

Rule 20: the genitive ἡμῶν is free — its only English is *our* — so it takes the determiner slot, the article realizes nothing, and *of* stays with the noun, as in τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ → *of his will*.
Source noun rendered *of + noun*, headed on the noun (rule 17); the case preposition rides with it under rule 20, discontinuously across *our* under rule 15.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive *our*.
Name split from κυρίου as separately recoverable (rules 17, 26).

review_notes: Reviewed the accepted alignment; returned unchanged except for one confidence correction at s012. All 21 source and 26 target IDs remain partitioned exactly once.

s012 raised from medium to high. It is the same construction as s002 — comparative adverb followed by an intensifying καί that the ASV renders *also* — and s002 was recorded high, so the two should not differ. Rule 82's correlative reading requires an English *so*, which the ASV writes in neither clause, and the old note's alternative (*even also* as one split frame) is not available, *even* standing beside *as* as καθάπερ's own gloss.

s018 τοῦ is the only unrepresented unit and is correct: rule 20 displacement by a free ἡμῶν → *our*, matching the contract's τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ → *of his will*, with *of* left on κυρίου. Rule 76's availability test is satisfied, ἡμῶν being spent on nothing else.

The verse's live question is the verbless comparative καθάπερ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἡμῶν → *even as ye also are ours*. I confirmed the supplied *are* on the predicate ἡμῶν: rule 56's spelled-out arm, καθὼς ἡμεῖς ἕν → *even as we are one*, is structurally identical, and rule 53's noun-phrase exception rests on an article-plus-noun predicate spelling itself out, which a single *ours* does not. s013 and s014 stay medium together, since the competing reading moves *are* between them.

ἀπὸ μέρους → *in part* correctly stays two units: rule 94 permits a compound prepositional unit only where the ASV writes a single English word, and rule 34's pleonastic case does not apply, *in* being a genuine English preposition answering to ἀπό under rule 36. Likewise ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ splits into *in* and *the*, the Greek preposition being expressed.
